assumptions: Currency is pounds (brief section 1: all amounts are in pounds; the API says arrears, min_due and monthly_repayment are in pounds). get_account and create_promise both use pounds as plain numbers (84.5 for £84.50), so amount_scale=1 and promise_scale=null. The brief gives no rounding rule, so promise_round=null.
Calendar: Monday to Friday are business days. The two holidays are 2026-11-27, which is a Friday, and 2026-12-21. So in the week of 2026-11-23 the last business day is Thursday 2026-11-26.

Bands: A is 1-10 days late, deadline the 12th business day after today, 1 proposal. B is 11-30, 9th business day, 2 proposals. C is 31-60, 7th business day, 3 proposals. D is 61-90, 5th business day, 4 proposals. 'Nth business day after today' never counts today. Worked example: today 2026-11-10 in band A gives 2026-11-26.

Rule 10 says the opening question 'Can you pay the full £{arrears} today?' is itself proposal 1 and counts toward the band total, so opening_is_attempt=true. Ladder step 1 is that opening ask (full arrears today). Steps 2-4 are the brief's Step 1 (full arrears on the last business day of the current week), Step 2 (full arrears on the deadline) and Step 3 (floor on the deadline). The band attempts are the brief's totals as given (A=1, B=2, C=3, D=4), so a band A customer who says no to the opening question has no proposals left.

Rule 12 says never make the same proposal twice; a step whose amount and date both match an earlier proposal is skipped, not said and not counted. Two cases: (a) if today is the last business day of the current week, the brief's Step 1 equals the opening ask and is skipped; (b) if the floor equals or exceeds the arrears, the floor-on-deadline step equals full-on-deadline and is skipped. The brief does not say to use next week's date when today is the week's last business day, so week_end_today=null and the duplicate is skipped instead.
Rule 13: when the band total is reached or the ladder runs out, stop proposing and close as no_agreement / refused. ladder_repeat_last=false.

Rule 7: the floor is min_due for store cards and monthly_repayment for personal and motor loans. The brief gives no clamp beyond 'never record less than the floor and never more than arrears', so a promise must satisfy floor <= amount <= arrears. If the floor is above the arrears, the arrears is the most that can be recorded.

Rule 6: a promise date must be a business day, not before today and not after the band's deadline. Deadlines computed as business days after today are always business days. previous_business_day is used for any other computed date that is not a business day, for example a Friday that is a holiday.

The brief does not say what to do when the customer says the full amount is too much. The default too_much_floor=attempt_1 is kept, and any floor proposal still counts against the band total (rule 11), with no new terms (rule 14).

Identity: birth_date first (sent YYYY-MM-DD), then postcode (sent in capitals with no spaces, so no space_before_last format). No fixed length is set because UK postcodes vary in length. Two wrong answers in total end the check, so max_wrong=2, closing as id_not_passed / failed. The API has no hint field, so hints={}. Unreadable answers come back ok=false and are not counted.

Opening: the brief says to tell the caller the call is recorded; this is said in active voice as 'We record this call.' The confirmation question is the brief's exact wording, 'Is this {title} {last_name}?'.

The brief never uses schedule_callback. Every weekday is set to null in callback.windows so no callback can be booked. When someone else answers on the customer's number, the agent closes without booking one.

The outcome table lists only wrong_number as a reason for not_contacted, so callback, no_callback, deceased and unclear (customer not reached or not confirmed) also close as not_contacted / wrong_number. id_declined (refusing the security questions) closes as id_not_passed / failed.
The brief never uses add_note, so notes.enabled=false and every note value is empty.

Transfers: hardship accepted goes to queue vulnerable_care, closing handed_over / care; hardship declined closes no_agreement / hardship. A payment plan request goes to repayment_plans, closing handed_over / plan. A request for a person goes to advisor, closing handed_over / advisor. Rule 19 says to transfer on request, so human.ask_first=false.

If create_promise fails twice, the call closes as no_agreement / system_error. The confirmation question is the brief's exact 'Is that right?'. The brief requires no SMS sentence, so sms_line is empty.

The brief is silent on the following, so defaults are used: date_rules next_weekday=following_week, confirm.max_asks=2, max_not_talk=2, purpose_is_decline=true, after_promise.ask_anything_else=true. Changing a recorded promise is also not covered, so the agent says it cannot be done on this call.
Floor spoken names ('minimum due', 'monthly repayment') come from the account field names; the brief calls both 'the floor'.
The brief does not say what happens to a days_late value outside 1-90, so bands_outside=null.
